guides.title: Redact a deposition exhibit
guides.answer: Redaction here deletes the text from the file, not just covers it with a black box — and the output is re-checked so the redacted words can't be extracted. For maximum certainty, turn on Rasterise pages: every page becomes an image, so no text layer survives at all.

guides.title: Combine exhibits into a filing-ready PDF
guides.answer: Upload your exhibits in order and get one document back: a slip sheet before each exhibit (Exhibit A, B, C… with filename and page count) and Bates numbers stamped continuously across every exhibit page.

guides.title: Compress a brief under your court's limit
guides.answer: Pick your court's size limit — 25 MB is the most common CM/ECF limit, but courts vary from about 3 to 200 MB, so check your local rule. The tool shrinks the file to fit and the ZIP includes a report showing the size before and after.

guides.title: Strip metadata before sending a document to the other side
guides.answer: A PDF can carry its author's name, creation dates and the software that made it. Strip Metadata removes all of it in one click and gives you a before/after report proving what was removed.

guides.title: Remove location data from case photos
guides.answer: Photos often carry GPS coordinates and camera details in their EXIF data. Strip Image Metadata lists what each photo carries, removes it, and reports what was taken out. Note: it does not verify removal of C2PA/AI markers — use ClearMark for those.

guides.title: Check what metadata a PDF you received contains
guides.answer: Before you rely on a document, see what's hidden in it. View Metadata reads the title, author, dates, creator and producer and gives you the result as JSON.

guides.title: Fix a document's title or author before filing
guides.answer: If a PDF's stored title or author is wrong — or names someone it shouldn't — Edit Metadata lets you set or clear the title, author, subject and keywords without touching the pages.

guides.title: Number the pages of a filing
guides.answer: Add page numbers in any corner, starting from any number, with a prefix or suffix if your court wants one. You can number only selected page ranges and leave the rest alone.

guides.title: Merge supporting documents into one bundle
guides.answer: Combine 2 to 20 PDFs into a single file in the order you upload them — pleadings, attachments and supporting documents as one bundle instead of many files.

guides.title: Pull one document out of a bundle
guides.answer: Split a PDF by page ranges (for example 1–3, 5) or into one file per page, and download the results as a ZIP. Useful when a bundle arrives as one file and you need a single exhibit from it.

guides.title: Protect a sensitive document with a password
guides.answer: Add a password to a PDF before sending it, so only someone with the password can open it. And if you receive a protected file and know the password, Unlock PDF removes the protection.

guides.title: Make a scanned document searchable
guides.answer: Scanned pages are pictures, not text — you can't search them or copy from them. OCR adds an invisible text layer so the document becomes searchable while looking exactly the same.

lawyers.limitsText: PDFEDI is a tool, not a lawyer. Court filing limits, redaction duties and disclosure rules vary by court and jurisdiction — check your court's local rules and your professional obligations before filing. Redaction here removes the text you name; always check the output before you file it. Files uploaded to these tools are processed on our server — see <link>how we handle your files</link>.

privacy.title: How we handle your files
privacy.intro: Plainly, without the usual privacy slogans. There are two different kinds of tools on PDFEDI, and they handle your files differently.
privacy.serverTitle: Server tools (most tools on this site)
privacy.serverText: When you use a tool like Merge, Redact or Compress, your file is uploaded to our server, processed there, and the result is sent back to you for download. Your file does leave your device — anyone who says otherwise about a server-processed tool is not telling you the truth. What we do promise:
serverPoints: No account, no sign-up, no email address asked for.
Files are processed automatically and deleted automatically.
Your file content is not kept, not shared with anyone, and not used to train anything.
We count anonymous usage (how many times a tool ran) so we can keep the free limits fair — we do not record what your files contain.
privacy.serverNote: Because these tools run on a server, the “airplane-mode test” does not apply to them: if you disconnect from the internet, a server tool cannot work at all. The checks that do apply here are the ones built into the tools themselves — for example, Redact re-checks its output so redacted text can't be extracted, and Strip Metadata gives you a before/after report showing exactly what was removed.
privacy.previewText: On the organizer tools (Merge, Split, Reorder, Delete, Rotate), the page thumbnails you see are rendered in your browser from the file on your device — no preview is uploaded to show them. Processing still happens on our server: when you press the process button, the file is uploaded, processed, and the result is sent back for download.
privacy.checkTitle: How to check our claims yourself

checkPoints.title: Redaction:
checkPoints.text: after redacting, try searching the output PDF for the redacted words — they should not be found. Turn on “Rasterise pages” and the output has no text layer at all.

checkPoints.title: Metadata:
checkPoints.text: open the metadata_report.json that comes with Strip Metadata, or use View Metadata on the cleaned file, and compare it with the original.

checkPoints.title: Previews:
checkPoints.text: open your browser's Network tab while arranging pages — no upload happens until you press the process button.

dontPoints: We don't sell or share your files.
We don't ask for an account to use the free tools.
We don't claim server-processed files “never leave your device” — they do, for processing, and then they're deleted.
privacy.localeNote: Your language preference is stored only in your own browser, so we can show you the site in your language next time. It is never sent to our servers.
